description: Ten simultaneous requests with the same Idempotency-Key: look for the key, create if missing
notes: Every request looked for the key before any of them had committed: none found it.
Ten purchases, ten charges, ten receipts and ten messages for one click.

description: Ten simultaneous requests with the same Idempotency-Key: unique (member, key) row, then wait for the answer
notes: One insert of the key committed; the other nine waited on the unique index, failed, and read the winner's purchase.
While the winner was charging, the others found its lease busy and waited for the answer.

description: 80 purchases while the provider takes 1.5 s; the call to the provider is inside the transaction

results.pool while the purchases wait for the pr: 60 active, 0 idle, 20 threads waiting for one
results.unrelated catalogue read at that moment: NO ANSWER within 500 ms (it answered after 1266 ms, once a purchase gave a connection back)

notes: Each purchase keeps its database connection while it waits for the provider: 60 connections busy doing nothing, the other requests wait for one.
The catalogue never talks to the provider, and it cannot answer either: it waits in the same queue for a connection.

description: 80 purchases while the provider takes 1.5 s; short transactions, the call outside any transaction

results.pool while the purchases wait for the pr: 0 active, 60 idle, 0 threads waiting for one

notes: While the purchases wait for the provider, they hold no connection: the pool is free.
Same pool, same provider, same timeouts: only the lifetime of the connection changed.

description: The provider charges the card but answers after 3 s; the shop gives up at 2 s and treats it as a failure
notes: The shop said 'payment failed' and put the book back on sale; the provider charged the card.
A retry with the same key finds the failed purchase: the member paid and has nothing.

description: The provider charges the card but answers after 3 s; the shop gives up at 2 s and treats it as unknown
notes: A timeout proves nothing: RECONCILE (202), and the book stays taken.
The retry sends the same provider key; the provider replays its stored answer: PAID, one receipt, one charge.

description: Something fails after the receipt is issued; the message was sent before the commit
notes: The transaction rolled back: no purchase, no receipt. The card was charged and the member was told about a receipt that does not exist.

description: Something fails after the receipt is issued; receipt and message are written in one transaction, sent after the commit
notes: The failure rolled back the receipt and its message together: nothing sent.
The provider had answered, so the purchase goes to RECONCILE, not FAILED; the retry settles it: one receipt, one message, one charge.

description: The application dies right after the purchase commits, before sending the message; then it comes back
notes: The message was committed with the receipt, so it survived the crash as a pending row.
The job sends it once; its next run finds nothing pending.
